svg.title: The three-party flow, with the four exchanges that touch your server
svg.desc: A sequence diagram with three lifelines: an MCP client in the host on the left, the MCP server acting as an OAuth 2.1 resource server in the middle and marked as your code, and an authorization server on the right. Four numbered exchanges run between the client and your server. One, a POST to the MCP endpoint with no Authorization header. Two, a 401 carrying a WWW-Authenticate challenge whose resource_metadata parameter is a URL. Three, a GET of the well-known protected-resource path, answered with a document holding resource, authorization_servers and more. Seven, the same POST repeated with a bearer token, answered 200, with a note that every later request runs the gate again. Between exchange three and exchange seven a shaded slab spans the client and authorization-server lifelines and holds exchanges four, five and six: authorization server metadata discovery, an authorize request carrying PKCE and a resource parameter that returns a code and an issuer, and a token exchange that returns a token audienced at you, with a note that the client compares the issuer byte for byte without normalizing it. The client and authorization server lifelines run straight through that slab. The MCP server lifeline stops at the top of it and resumes below it, because your server is in none of those three exchanges. A band at the foot states the resource server's entire job: publish the metadata, answer 401 with a challenge that points at it, and validate every token for signature, expiry, audience and scope, never issuing one and never forwarding one.
svg.text: One token, three parties, and the small part that is yours
Four of the seven exchanges touch your server. It validates a token it never issued.
the client and the authorization server, alone
/token + code_verifier -> a token audienced at you
the client compares iss byte for byte; no normalization
200 every later request runs the gate again
publish the metadata, answer 401 with a challenge that points at it, validate every token
signature, expiry, audience, scope. Never issue one, never forward one.
